title: Online Test Proctoring Assistance
summary: Flag possible malpractice in remote tests from webcam frames and browser events, so a trained proctor reviews short evidence clips and decides, rather than software disqualifying students.

seo.title: AI Proctoring Assistance for Online Tests | VipraTech
seo.description: Computer vision that flags absent faces, extra people, phones and tab switches in remote tests, with proctors reviewing evidence before any action.

problem.intro: Online scholarship tests, mock tests and university semester exams let students sit from home, but institutions still need confidence in the result. Live human proctoring does not scale to thousands of candidates, and many off-the-shelf tools flag so much that proctors stop trusting them, or penalise students for things they cannot control.

pain_points.title: Too few proctors per candidate
pain_points.detail: One invigilator can watch only a handful of video tiles, so most of a large remote test goes effectively unwatched.

pain_points.title: False flags from real homes
pain_points.detail: Shared rooms, poor lighting, low-end webcams and patchy bandwidth produce flags that have nothing to do with cheating.

pain_points.title: No usable evidence
pain_points.detail: When a result is challenged, the institution often has a risk score but no clip or timeline showing what actually happened.

pain_points.title: Privacy concerns from parents
pain_points.detail: Continuous recording of minors at home raises questions about consent, storage and who can watch the footage.

solution.overview: We build a proctoring assistant that sits alongside your test platform. Before the test it compares the candidate's face with the registered photo and records a short room check. During the test it samples webcam frames and browser events and runs detectors for an absent face, more than one person, a phone or book in view, repeated looking away and window switching. Detections are grouped into time-stamped incidents with short clips, not a single opaque score. A proctor reviews each incident and records a decision; the system never ends a test or disqualifies a candidate on its own.
capabilities: Pre-test identity check against the registered photo, with a manual fallback
Detectors for an absent face, multiple people, phones and printed material in view
Browser event capture: tab or window switches, copy-paste attempts and full-screen exits
Incident timeline with short clips and frames instead of one opaque risk score
Light on-device processing with snapshot upload for low-bandwidth candidates
Configurable retention, after which frames and clips are deleted automatically

workflow.title: Consent and set-up
workflow.detail: The candidate, or a parent for a minor, sees what is captured and why, and the system checks camera, microphone and connection.

workflow.title: Identity and room check
workflow.detail: A face capture is compared with the registered photo and a short room scan is recorded.

workflow.title: Monitor during the test
workflow.detail: Webcam frames and browser events are sampled and passed through the detectors throughout the test.

workflow.title: Build incidents
workflow.detail: Detections that cross agreed thresholds are grouped into incidents with time stamps and clips.

workflow.title: Proctor review
workflow.detail: A proctor watches each incident, marks it as no issue, warning or escalate, and adds a note.

workflow.title: Report to the exam controller
workflow.detail: Escalated incidents and their evidence go to the exam controller, who decides any action after hearing the candidate.

inputs: Registered candidate photo from admission or test registration
Webcam frames and optional audio during the test
Proctoring policy with thresholds agreed by the exam controller
outputs: Incident timeline per candidate with clips and frames
Escalation report for the exam controller
Test-level summary of incidents by type
human_in_the_loop: A trained proctor reviews every incident before anything is recorded against a candidate, and only the exam controller can take action, after giving the candidate a chance to explain. Thresholds are tuned with the exam cell so the number of incidents stays reviewable.
integrations: Online test or CBT platform (via SDK or API)
Student information system for registered photos
Single sign-on for students and proctors
Cloud storage in an India region
Email or WhatsApp for candidate notices
guardrails: No automatic disqualification, test termination or score change
Clear notice and consent before capture, with parental consent for minors
Face data used only for that test's identity check, not kept as a biometric profile
Thresholds reviewed for false flags across lighting, devices and bandwidth
Clips deleted automatically after the agreed retention period
compliance_notes: The DPDP Act 2023 restricts tracking and behavioural monitoring of children; proctoring for minors should be limited to the test window and purpose, with parental consent.
For candidates in Europe, GDPR treats biometric data used for identification as special-category data, so a lawful basis and impact assessment are needed.

pilot.scope: One online test series, such as a scholarship or mock test, with proctors reviewing AI incidents alongside their current method.
deliverables: Proctoring policy and thresholds agreed with the exam cell
Integration with your test platform for the pilot test
False-flag analysis across devices and conditions
Recommendation on roll-out, retention and staffing

what_we_measure.how: Share of incidents marked warning or escalate rather than no issue.
Incidents marked no issue, broken down by lighting, device type and bandwidth.
Average time to review one incident, from console logs.
Candidates who could not complete the test because of the client, from support tickets.

faqs.q: Will the system disqualify students automatically?
faqs.a: No. It only creates incidents with evidence. A proctor reviews each one, and any action is taken by the exam controller after the candidate has been heard.

faqs.q: Does it work on low-end laptops and slow connections?
faqs.a: It is designed to. Basic face detection can run on the device, and only snapshots are uploaded when bandwidth is low. The pilot measures how many candidates face technical problems so you can set minimum requirements.

faqs.q: What about bias and false flags?
faqs.a: Detectors can perform worse in poor lighting or with some cameras. We measure false flags across conditions during the pilot, tune thresholds with your exam cell and keep a human review on every incident.
As long as you decide, usually until the result appeal window closes. Deletion is automatic and logged, and access to clips is restricted and recorded.
